moments.title: The numbers behind the US-Venezuela oil deal: Venezuela has now confirmed that the agreement covers 65 billion barrels of oil across 17 fields, with the US receiving "majority control." At current WTI crude oil prices of
moments.selftext: The numbers behind the US-Venezuela oil deal: Venezuela has now confirmed that the agreement covers 65 billion barrels of oil across 17 fields, with the US receiving "majority control." At current WTI crude oil prices of ~$83/barrel, those reserves have a gross market value of ~$5.4 trillion. Reports indicate the deal includes 100-year rights to develop the fields, while the US will receive 55% effective output, along with an ownership stake and rights to purchase oil at cost. At 55%, that would correspond to ~35.8 billion barrels of effective output. At today’s oil prices, that amount of crude alone has a gross market value of ~$3 trillion. That said, Venezuela primarily produces heavy, sour crude, which typically trades at a meaningful discount to benchmark oil prices and requires more expensive production, blending, and refining. Even assuming an illustrative $25-$35 of net economic value per barrel after discounts and development/operating costs, ~35.8 billion barrels could represent up to ~$1.25 trillion of cumulative economic value over the life of the fields. This includes a $100 billion investment to develop these fields, while Venezuela estimates the projects will generate $209 billion in tax revenue for the country. This is one of the biggest energy deals in history.

moments.title: An Italian politician brought her 44-day-old daughter to work and continued bringing her to work for the next three years. Italian politician Licia Ronzulli famously brought her 44-day-old daughter, Vittoria, to the Euro
moments.selftext: An Italian politician brought her 44-day-old daughter to work and continued bringing her to work for the next three years. Italian politician Licia Ronzulli famously brought her 44-day-old daughter, Vittoria, to the European Parliament in September 2010. As a breastfeeding mother without dedicated childcare facilities at work, she carried her baby in a sling while participating in parliamentary voting sessions. Vittoria continued accompanying her mother to the chamber for the next three years, becoming a familiar sight in Parliament. As she grew older, she even began playfully raising her hand alongside her mother, mimicking Ronzulli during votes.

moments.selftext: BREAKING: US M2 money supply surged +$102.8 billion in July, to a record $23.22 trillion. This marks the 27th consecutive monthly increase. Since the start of 2026, M2 has now risen +$862.7 billion. Furthermore, money supply now stands $1.43 trillion above the March 2022 peak. Since 2000, money in circulation has grown at an average annual rate of +6.3%, or ~$700 billion a year. US money creation is expanding at a rapid pace.

moments.title: In 1980, an 8-year-old boy discovered $5,800 of D. B. Cooper’s ransom money decomposing along the banks of the Columbia River, more than eight years after the hijacker disappeared. On November 24, 1971, a man calling him
moments.selftext: In 1980, an 8-year-old boy discovered $5,800 of D. B. Cooper’s ransom money decomposing along the banks of the Columbia River, more than eight years after the hijacker disappeared. On November 24, 1971, a man calling himself Dan Cooper hijacked Northwest Orient Flight 305, demanding $200,000 and four parachutes. After the plane took off, he eventually jumped from the Boeing 727 somewhere over the Pacific Northwest and vanished without a trace. Neither Cooper nor the vast majority of the ransom was ever recovered. Then, in February 1980, eight-year-old Brian Ingram was vacationing with his family at Tena Bar along the Columbia River in Washington. While digging in the sand, he uncovered three deteriorating bundles of $20 bills totaling $5,800. The FBI confirmed that the serial numbers matched the ransom money given to Cooper, making it the only portion of the ransom ever recovered. How the money ended up buried along the riverbank remains a mystery. The FBI officially closed its active investigation in 2016 after 45 years, having pursued hundreds of suspects without conclusively determining Cooper’s identity. More than five decades later, no one knows for certain who D. B. Cooper really was—or whether he survived the jump.
